guide.summary: After Jesus' ascension, the Holy Spirit descended at Pentecost transforming timid disciples into courageous apostles. The early Church was born with power, unity and authenticity, growing exponentially despite persecution.

guide.summary: Peter was transformed from a man who denied Jesus into a courageous leader of the Church. John was his faithful companion. Stephen was the first martyr, demonstrating that faith is worth more than life. These heroes teach us about courage, faithfulness and sacrifice.

exercises.explanation: Peter's transformation is dramatic: from denier to bold preacher.

guide.summary: Saul was persecuting Christians when Jesus encountered him on the Damascus road. Transformed into apostle Paul, he traveled throughout the Greco-Roman world founding churches. His letters continue to guide Christian faith today.

exercises.explanation: Saul was zealously fighting against the Church when his encounter with Jesus changed everything.

exercises.statement: Jesus personally appeared to Saul on the Damascus road.
exercises.explanation: The risen Jesus Himself appeared to Saul, asking why he persecuted Him.

units.subtitle: Paul in Rome and His Letters

guide.summary: Paul's letters written during his ministry contain the essence of Christian faith. Romans 8 speaks of hope in Christ, 1 Corinthians 13 exalts love, Philippians 4 teaches joy, Galatians 5 speaks of freedom, Ephesians 6 about the armor of God. These continue to transform lives.

keyVerses.text: And we know that in all things God works for good with those who love him.
Love is patient and kind; love is not envious.
Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of his might.

exercises.text: "And we know that in all things God works for good with those who love _____."
exercises.speaker: Paul
exercises.explanation: Paul affirms that God works all circumstances for good for those who love Him.

exercises.statement: Romans 8:28 means the Christian life will have no difficulties.
exercises.explanation: The verse does not say there will be no difficulties, but that God works in them for good.

exercises.prompt: What is the central message of Romans 8?

exercises.answer: Nothing can separate us from God's love in Christ

lessons.title: Review - Paul in Rome and His Letters

exercises.prompt: What is the importance of Paul's letters?
exercises.text: His writings defined Christian theology for centuries.
options: They comprise half the New Testament and guide Christian faith
They have no value for modern Christians
They were discarded by the Church
exercises.answer: They comprise half the New Testament and guide Christian faith
exercises.explanation: Paul's 13 letters are essential for understanding Christian faith.

exercises.statement: All of Paul's letters address specific problems in local churches.
exercises.explanation: Paul wrote to specific churches and individuals, but his lessons are universal.

exercises.prompt: What is the central theme of Paul's letters?
exercises.text: Despite variety, there is a thematic unity.
options: Salvation in Christ and life transformed by the Spirit
exercises.answer: Salvation in Christ and life transformed by the Spirit
exercises.explanation: Christ and transformation by His Spirit are the heart of all Paul writes.
